Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, down from 33% last season.

Michael Eyssimont returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

story.head: Pastrňák’s favorite opponent
paras: The Bruins have won four straight, while the Canadiens (11-3-4) lost 2-1 in overtime to Minnesota on Tuesday. Two of the league’s best teams meet. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Habs third (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Bruins first (fifth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Canadiens’ record (.722) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.561), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games. So is the Bruins’ (.750 on chances worth .564), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th), so the Bruins could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), so the Canadiens’ defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. Boston has allowed 2.28 goals a game, the second fewest in the league.

Lane Hutson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Cole Caufield (11 G / 6 A / 17 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with a point in seven straight games against Boston. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 18 GP), who has a point in eleven straight games against Montréal.

Jacob Fowler (8-1-2 / .925 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and is expected to start. Jeremy Swayman (9-3-1 / .920 SV% in 13 GS) has been a rock in net for Boston and is expected to start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.
